Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the EcoNova Renewables Inc. Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. During the Q&A session, please press star then one on your touchtone phone to ask a question. To withdraw your question, press star then two. We ask that you limit yourself to one question and one follow-up. As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss EcoNova Renewables' results for the second quarter of 2024. Joining me on today's call are Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Executive Officer; Marcus Hale, Chief Financial Officer; Lila Chen, Chief Development Officer; Dr. Raj Patel, Chief Technology Officer; Sofia Grant, Chief Sustainability Officer; Tom Reilly, Chief Operating Officer; Nina Kowalski, Chief Strategy Officer; and Victor Lang, Chief Risk Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements. We encourage you to review the disclaimer in our press release and on our website regarding these statements.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Vasquez.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. EcoNova Renewables continues to demonstrate its leadership in the renewable energy sector, achieving a record-breaking performance in Q2. Our success is a testament to our unwavering commitment to innovation, sustainability, and operational excellence.

Today, I want to highlight eight key aspects of our performance that underscore this momentum. First, our disciplined approach to capital expenditures and operating expenses, which supports scaling our portfolio while driving down costs. Second, the supportive policy and regulatory environment accelerating our deployments globally. Third, our prudent management of debt levels and financing costs amid market volatility. Fourth, robust additions to our development pipeline and achievement of critical project milestones. Fifth, innovative tax equity and project-level financing unlocking liquidity. Sixth, strong progress on construction and adherence to commercial operation dates. Seventh, exceptional revenue and earnings growth driven by diversified segments. And eighth, favorable PPA pricing trends and successful contract extensions providing revenue stability.

These elements position us for sustained growth. Now, I'll hand the call over to Marcus to provide a detailed review of our financial results.

Marcus Hale:
Thank you, Elena. Our financial performance in Q2 was exceptional. Revenue reached $1.42 billion, representing a 38% increase compared to the same period last year. This growth was driven by significant project commissioning and increased energy production across our solar PV, onshore wind, BESS, and emerging green hydrogen segments. Our gross margin expanded to 28.5%, reflecting improved operational efficiency, cost management, and scale in manufacturing. Operating expenses totaled $187 million, or 18% of revenue, primarily due to investments in R&D, sales and marketing, and cybersecurity. Net income was $210 million, or $0.92 diluted earnings per share. We ended the quarter with $420 million in cash and cash equivalents, bolstering our liquidity to $3.1 billion including undrawn facilities. We are significantly raising our full-year guidance for revenue to $5.6-5.8 billion and adjusted EBITDA to $1.15-1.20 billion.

Let me expand on some of those key aspects Elena mentioned, starting with our CAPEX and OPEX details, which are cornerstones of scaling our 5.2 GW portfolio of utility-scale solar, onshore wind, and BESS while pushing weighted average LCOE under $25 per MWh. In Q2, we deployed $428 million in CAPEX, bringing H1 total to $812 million—a 28% year-over-year increase—on track for our $2.8 billion full-year guidance, front-loaded toward back-half construction. Project development and EPC took 62%, or $265 million, funding the 450 MW Desert Sun Solar PV in Arizona and 300 MW Prairie Wind Farm Phase II in Texas, with fixed-price EPC contracts from Turner Renewable Energy shielding against easing steel and copper inflation—down 12% from Q4 2023 peaks despite China's 80% polysilicon dominance. Energy storage and grid integration claimed 24%, or $103 million, for our 1.2 GWh BESS pipeline, including a 200 MW/800 MWh hybrid at Mojave Solar using CATL LFP packs at a 15% YoY cost cut to $65/kWh ex-factory. R&D got the rest, $60 million, advancing perovskite-silicon tandem modules to 28.5% lab efficiency with Oxford PV, eyeing $0.20/Wp by decade's end.

U.S. CAPEX led at 68%, boosted by IRA ITCs at 45% for solar-plus-storage and PTC extensions lifting IRRs to 12-14%. Europe was 22% with €120 million in Spanish PV under REPowerEU, justified by €200/MWh Iberian peaks. APAC at 10% focused on Vietnam localization against U.S. tariffs. Q3-Q4 CAPEX accelerates to $1.0-1.2 billion with a buffer for Vestas turbine delays, yielding 9.2% ROIC on incremental spend versus 7.8% last year, backed by 85% PPAs at $35-45/MWh fixed for 15+ years.

On OPEX, Q2's $187 million aligned with $720-760 million full-year guidance, up just 4% YoY despite 22% portfolio growth, dropping cash OPEX per MW 11% to $14,200 annually below Lazard benchmarks. O&M was 48% or $90 million across 4.8 GW: solar flat at $8/kW/year via drone cleaning and AI soiling prediction cutting Texas downtime 22%; wind up 6% to $22/kW/year for Siemens Gamesa inspections but GE Vernova analytics slashed outages 35%; BESS at $4.5/kW/year with 95% warranties and proprietary EMS. SG&A and corporate 28% or $52 million, down 2% as revenue percent, including $15 million cybersecurity for IEC 62443 and $8 million ERCOT talent. The balance covered $45 million amortized development for our 10+ GW pipeline in PJM and CAISO.

OPEX margins improved 210 bps to 82% EBITDA, via scale and digital twins trimming wind wake losses 8%. U.S. OPEX leverages ERCOT/SPP ancillaries adding $22 million Q2 uplift; Europe offsets 9% labor hikes with ETS credits; Australia uses falling diesel for microgrids. OPEX-to-CAPEX under 25% by 2025, funded by $1.2 billion green bonds at 4.8% and $500 million revolver, hedging rates with 70% fixed debt amid IEA's $1.7 trillion clean CAPEX wave. Labor shortages and module times are risks, buffered by 18-month inventory and First Solar/Trina multi-sourcing.

Turning to revenue and earnings growth, this 38% YoY jump to $1.42 billion beat guidance by 8%, with 12% QoQ growth and 11th straight double-digit quarter outpacing BloombergNEF's 25% solar market. Adjusted EBITDA rose 52% to $285 million at 20.1% margins, up 320 bps on 15% polysilicon drop to $8.50/kg. Non-GAAP EPS doubled to $0.92 from $0.45.

Solar PV, 72% of revenue at $1.02 billion, grew 42% on 4.2 GWdc shipments of 23.8% efficient TOPCon bifacials, IRA domestic content certified, with U.S. utility PPAs to NextEra/Duke; margins to 28.5% via Arizona Fab-3 at $0.22/W. BESS, 18% or $256 million, exploded 65% on 1.8 GWh including CAISO data center wins with NVIDIA-tied EMS; margins 22% from Nevada gigafactory and cheap LFP. Green H2/services 10% at $164 million up 25%, shipping 50 MW PEM to Ørsted-led EU consortium.

North America 55% ($781 million, +48%) via $12 billion IRA ITCs and CA 52 GW target; Europe 28% (+32%) on EEG/CfD; APAC 15% (+18%) with Adani JV/PLI; Brazil added distributed solar. Trends: BoM costs down 18% to $0.19/W via copper plating/kerf savings; 85% compliant supply chain; HJT/VFB pilots for DOE grants; data center 25% bookings. Cash flow $320 million funded $450 million capex; leverage 1.2x; FCF yield 8%+ supports $0.15 dividend.

On debt levels and financing costs, total gross debt $5.2 billion down from $5.5 billion YE23 via $350 million paydowns; net debt $4.78 billion at 4.1x ttm EBITDA, in 3.5-4.5x target, better than NextEra/Ørsted peers, with long-term fixed-rate suiting 15 GW portfolio cash flows. Cost of debt 4.3%, down 60 bps YoY: refinanced $800 million Term Loan B to SOFR+140 bps sustainability-linked loan; $1 billion 12-year green bond at 3.75% (+95 bps Treasuries) with $4 billion demand/greenium. U.S. 55% backlog 70% non-recourse PF with IRA PTC/ITC, e.g., $650 million Rattlesnake loan SOFR+165 bps. Europe 30% EIB-backed; APAC 15% sukuk. 85% fixed beyond 2025; FFO/debt 18%; 'Match-Maturity' aligns tenors to 18-year PPAs; battery recycling venture debt; $1.5 billion eyed for H2.

For tax equity and project-level financing, YTD $1.4 billion tax equity across eight projects, 65% of 2024 U.S. CODs. Q2 Desert Sun flip $620 million from JPM/US Bancorp at 8.5% IRR, post-flip 65% upside at $28/MWh LCOE. IRA transferability boosts liquidity to $25 billion+ market. Project finance $2.1 billion at SOFR+175 bps blended 5.8%: Atlantic Breeze $1.2 billion DNB/ING; Texas BESS $450 million 1.8x DSCR. Stack: 40-50% tax equity, 50-60% debt, 10-20% sponsor at 5.2% WACC. Corporates 30%; PACE pilots; APAC JPY PF. Target $3.5-4 billion 2025 for 2 GW adds.

Finally, PPA pricing trends and extensions: 85% backlog contracted, avg 12.3 years. Q3 new 1.2 GW, extended 800 MW. Solar avg $28/MWh +3% QoQ/-7% YoY on $0.22/W modules/LCOE <$25; wind onshore $32/MWh +5% YoY; offshore $65/MWh; hybrids $42/MWh +12%. ERCOT sub-$25; CAISO $35 +LCFS; Europe €42-£47; Aus AUD65. Escalators 2.2%; extensions 18% premium e.g., CA solar $40 to $48/MWh +storage. Blended $35/MWh 70% fixed; 70% 2026-28 maturities targeted 15-20% uplifts. Solar $26-30/MWh 2025, hybrids $40+.

I'll now turn the call over to Lila to discuss our project development activities.

Lila Chen:
Thank you, Marcus. Our project development pipeline continues to grow rapidly, now totaling 28.4 GW across renewables—up 22% YoY—for 4-5 GW annual adds through 2027. Q2 added 4.2 GW to late-stage 12.1 GW, strongest since Q4 2022 via origination, M&A, leases. Solar 2.1 GWdc (SunForge 500 Arizona 1.2 GWdc 32% CF TOPCon/Nextracker +IRA adders 12-14% IRR); onshore wind 1.4 GW (Prairie Winds OK 850 MW Vestas V162-6.2 MW 50-55% CF +400 MWh BESS); BESS/hybrids 500 MW/1.8 GWh (200 MWh Form Energy LDES <$250/kWh); offshore/H2 early 200 MW CA float/50 MW TX electrolyzer.

U.S. 65% (2.7 GW +$1.2 billion IRA credits); Europe 25% (REPowerEU/CfD); APAC 10% (India Adani). Milestones: 18 keys advancing 3.2 GW. FIDs 1.8 GW (SunRise TX 1.2 GWdc+600 MWh Google PPA $35/MWh $450 million tax equity 11.8% IRR; Gale Force IL 600 MW MISO/GE); NTP/starts 1.1 GW (Horizon CA BESS 400 MW/1.6 GWh Tesla Q4 COD $100+/MWh); PPAs 2.3 GW 80% corporate (MSFT 500 MW; Air Products H2 $3.50/kg); permits 800 MW SW; UK East Anglia TSO; VFB pilot Aus 95% RTE. 70% Tier 1 markets, top-queue; 95% fixed EPC; 60% U.S. content. Q3/Q4 4-5 GW adds, 2 GW FID; $2.5 billion liquidity.

Dr. Raj Patel, can you update us on our technological advancements?

Dr. Raj Patel:
Thank you, Lila. We are committed to driving innovation in the renewable energy sector. Our R&D efforts are focused on groundbreaking technologies enhancing efficiency, reliability, and affordability—like perovskite tandems at 28.5%, HJT 26%, VFB 4-hour, AI EMS, copper plating, dynamic line rating, and EMS for thermal runaway. Partnerships with LONGi, Trina, CATL, Oxford PV, Form Energy position us to revolutionize energy with LCOE <$25/MWh and LDES at $250/kWh.

Next, Sofia will discuss our sustainability initiatives.

Sofia Grant:
Thank you, Raj. Sustainability is deeply ingrained in our corporate culture, and we are committed to minimizing our environmental impact and contributing to a more sustainable future. We have ambitious goals for carbon reductions, energy efficiency, and resource management, aligned with SBTi Scope 1/2 targets. Community engagement, circular BESS recycling, blockchain polysilicon traceability, and ETS credits support this, while EU Taxonomy and IRA compliance drive ESG-linked financing.

Now, Tom will provide operational highlights.

Tom Reilly:
Thank you, Sofia. Our operational performance remains exceptional. We are optimizing operations across 4.8 GW with best-in-class asset management, maintenance, and supply chain—drone/AI O&M cutting downtime 22-35%, digital twins 8% wake savings, 98% CF targets. Training investments ensure excellence; 92% on-time milestones via in-house EPC, First Solar/Vestas ties. Construction: Desert Bloom CA 650 MWdc 78% (Q1 2025 COD SCE PPA $28/MWh); Lone Star TX 1.2 GW hybrid 65% (Q2 2025 COD); Vanguard AZ BESS 90% (Q3 2024 COD $250/kW-year); UK North Sea 55% (H2 2026 CfD £44/MWh); Pilbara H2 88% (Q4 2025). 2.8 GW FY25 CODs +$450 million EBITDA; 25 GW backlog +18% QoQ.

Nina, can you provide an update on our strategic initiatives?

Nina Kowalski:
Thank you, Tom. We are executing our long-term plan: market expansion, product diversification, partnerships. Policy tailwinds amplify this—U.S. IRA $1.2 billion credits, 45X/PTC/ITC to 40%, state LCFS/ERCOT adding $67 million EBITDA, FERC 2023 queues; Europe REPowerEU/Fit55 €320 million IPCEI, H2 Bank €1.2/kg, ETS €85/t; China dual carbon/Golden Sun, India PLI 5 GW; Brazil/Aus auctions. 78% pipeline de-risked, 22% IRR boost, 65% corporate PPAs, storage mandates. Lobbying $15 million, AI curtailment, H2Hubs; 60/40 split buffers risks.

And finally, Victor, can you address our risk management strategies?

Victor Lang:
Thank you, Nina. We have robust strategies mitigating market, regulatory, environmental risks—monitoring queues, inflation (EPC fixed-price), supply (multi-source/inventory), rates (70% fixed/swaps), geopolitics (localization), permitting (pre-compliance), cyber (IEC), elections (lock-ins). Liquidity $3.1 billion, A- rating provide resilience for $1.7 trillion clean spend.

I'll turn it back to Elena for closing remarks.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you all. In conclusion, EcoNova Renewables had a truly exceptional Q2. We are confident that our strategic initiatives, commitment to innovation, and focus on sustainability will drive long-term growth and success.

Operator, let's proceed with the Q&A session.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, if you wish to ask a question, please press star then one. Our first question comes from Ben Thompson with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Ben Thompson:
What are your plans for investing in new technologies such as green hydrogen?

Dr. Raj Patel:
Thanks, Ben. Green hydrogen is a priority in our innovation pipeline. We've added 50 MW electrolyzer capacity like H2 Horizon in Texas with ITM Power PEM fed by curtailed renewables, and Pilbara Hub with Plug Power targeting 50,000 tonnes/year off-take to Rio Tinto. Investments align with DOE H2Hubs and EU Hydrogen Bank, aiming $3/kg at scale by 2027 via 300 MW pilots, 45V PTC, and solar/wind integration for 18% IRR uplift. We're scaling to 10% revenue by 2026 with electrolyzer costs below $400/kW.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Park with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Lisa Park:
How are you managing the increasing competition in the renewable energy market?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Great question, Lisa. Competition is intensifying, but our edge lies in tech leadership—28.5% tandems, AI optimization, LDES—and execution: top-quartile queues, 95% fixed EPC, 60% U.S. content for IRA, diversified 28.4 GW pipeline 70% Tier 1. Corporate PPAs 65-80%, vertical integration (fabs, blades), and financing prowess (WACC 5.2%) deliver superior IRRs 12-14%, outpacing peers. We're shaping markets via advocacy and partnerships like CATL, Vestas, Google.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Rivera with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Mike Rivera:
Can you discuss the potential impact of climate change on your operations?

Victor Lang:
Absolutely, Mike. Climate change poses risks like extreme weather, but we mitigate proactively. Hurricane Beryl delayed Lone Star minimally via resilient design; AI soiling/predictive O&M cuts downtime; BESS/LDES address duck curves/curtailment (12% ERCOT). Repowering boosts CF 24-28%; blockchain traceability, circular recycling enhance resilience. Upside: LCFS/RNG $185/MTCO2e adds $67 million; we're SBTi-aligned, EU Taxonomy/ESG-linked debt for adaptation funding.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sarah Lee with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Sarah Lee:
What are your expectations for the long-term profitability of your renewable energy projects?

Marcus Hale:
Thanks, Sarah. Long-term profitability is strong, with unlevered IRRs 11.8-14%, ROIC 9.2-20%, EBITDA margins 82% via LCOE <$25/MWh, hybrids $42/MWh PPAs, escalators 2.2%, extensions 15-20% uplifts. 85% contracted 12-18 years, stacking ITC/PTC/LCFS/ancillaries; 60% gross margins FY25. Policy de-risks 78% pipeline, FCF CAGR 25%, dividend sustainable at 15% yield. Peers like NextEra validate as renewables hit LCOE parity.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, there appear to be no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back over to Dr. Vasquez for any closing remarks.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you all for your participation in today's call. We appreciate your continued support of EcoNova Renewables. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
